# Anantarāpayuttakathā (Kv 13.3)

**ID:** Kv 13.3  
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)  
**Collection:** Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Anantarāpayuttakathā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul20.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul20.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anantarāpayuttakathā* (Kv 13.3) is the third discourse of the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, located in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The debate concerns the status of an individual bound to an immediate destiny (*anantarāpayutta puggala*)—specifically someone guilty of one of the grave offenses entailing immediate retribution (*anantaravipāka*), such as matricide, parricide, murdering an arahant, shedding the blood of a Buddha, or causing a schism in the Saṅgha—and investigates whether such a person is capable or incapable of entering the assurance of correctness (*sammattaniyāma*) [Bareau 1955]. In his study of early Buddhist schools, André Bareau notes sectarian positions regarding whether this individual can enter the path of right determination or is definitively precluded from it [Bareau 1955].

**Sources**

- [Bareau 1955] André Bareau, Les sectes bouddhiques du Petit Véhicule (1955) — Contextualized the debate regarding whether an anantarāpayutta individual can enter into the sammattaniyāma and clarified the nature of the offenses.
